maria_support: FYI — customer 'acme' reports intermittent 403s immediately after we rotated their API key this morning. Some requests still succeed for a while. attaching short timeline and errors.

alex_platform: which clients are failing? mobile, server, edge? any request ids?

maria_support: Mostly server-to-server jobs in eu-west and a couple of webhook retries. errors are 403 with body: \"invalid api key\". Successful requests are coming through our edge and appear to have a different key in the Authorization header. No request ids in the app logs (they're 3rd party).

ingrid_ops: quick hypothesis: rotation wrote new secret to Vault, but some pods/sidecars didn't pick up updated envvar. Also our edge has header caching/normalization with a 5m TTL; if an old key was seen there it could still be forwarded.

maria_support: repro steps from customer: 
1) rotated key via console (kv path: secret/data/apps/acme/apikey)
2) updated service account in their infra with new value (they claim)
3) within 2m some webhooks failed with 403, but other requests passed.

alex_platform: can we get a packet or headers example? if frontend passes old header, that indicates client-side cache. if backend keepalive reused old Authorization on connection pool, that's another bug.

maria_support: customer provided one curl they used after rotation: 

```
curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer <NEW_KEY_PLACEHOLDER>\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/engines
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
content-type: application/json
{ \"error\": \"invalid api key\" }
```

then a different curl from same IP succeeded ~30s later with header showing different key in logs (we asked them to mask).

taylor_eng: digging into infra: we saw a pattern last week — our long-lived HTTP clients (connection pools in our worker fleet) stash the Authorization header on first request and reuse it for keep-alive connections unless a reconnect occurs. If a key changes underneath, those connections still carry old auth. That matches short window of mixed success/fail.

ingrid_ops: also saw that our sidecar secret injector (vault-agent) refresh interval default is 300s unless forced. If service uses envvar injection without SIGHUP to reload process, app will keep old secret. Combine that with connection-pool header reuse and edge cache TTL and you get this exact mix.

maria_support: customer says they rotated via Vault UI and updated k8s secret values, but didn't restart deployments. they assumed rolling update would pick it up.

alex_platform: recommended immediate mitigation steps: 
- force restart affected deployments: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/<name>` to ensure envvars refreshed and processes pick up new key.
- flush edge header cache / purge CDN for that route (we have admin api: POST /admin/edge/purge with route) to evict cached auth normalization.
- on any long-lived worker: restart or drain connections so pools re-establish using current env.

taylor_eng: debug commands we ran in cluster: 
```
# check vault-agent files inside pod
kubectl exec -it pod/<pod> -c vault-agent -- cat /etc/secrets/acme_api_key
# force reload sidecar
kubectl exec -it pod/<pod> -c vault-agent -- kill -HUP 1
# show http conn reuse in metrics
kubectl logs pod/<pod> | grep \"keep-alive reused auth\"
```

ingrid_ops: ops performed a targeted restart and triggered CDN purge for the customer's route ~6m after rotation. customer confirmed failures stopped within 90s after those actions.

maria_support: resolution summary for ticket: 
- root cause: rotation created new key, but app processes and connection pools continued to use the old key (envvar not reloaded + connection reuse) and edge/CDN had TTL for header normalization.
- immediate fix: restart deployments + purge CDN + restart long-lived workers.
- recommended changes: update rotation runbook to include: 
  * post-rotation: force SIGHUP or rollout restart for pods using env-injected keys
  * drain/recreate connection pools for stateful workers or add health-check-triggered reconnect
  * call CDN admin purge after rotation to avoid 5m stale window
  * add a short-lived grace binding: accept previous key for X seconds only if rotating (to avoid 0s cutover) OR implement token versioning so old connections can be invalidated centrally.

taylor_eng: follow-ups: 
- we'll add a kv version check in our vault sync lambda to emit an alert if a secret update doesn't propagate to >90% pods in 2m.
- platform will add a `rotation` flag to our deploy tool that does automated restarts + optional CDN purge.

ops_bot: trigger: deploybot started: redeploy/support-rotation-fix by taylor_eng (run id: 2027-09-12-42) :rocket:

maria_support: tagging ticket as resolved with notes and runbook updates. customer happy for now, wants a postmortem tech note. I'll loop in product + eng for runbook changes. :thumbsup:
